notes.body: added this merge request to the [merge train](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_trains) at position 2
How is this fix better when we're actively trying to eliminate snprintf calls?

okay, I was not aware of that activity to eliminate `snprintf()` calls.

The reason I used this way to fix Coverity warnings. I tested and it works (warning was cleared for me in my test).

I can change back to use wmem functions, using NULL allocator and `wmem_free(NULL, ...)`, if that is what you prefer.

What I get frustrated with is blindly believing Coverity (and not understanding the Wireshark API enough to know why).  I really do appreciate the effort you're putting into this, but it seems like Coverity does not understand how wmem or the API of the epan directory works.  So the result is making dissector code "more complicated" to address false positives.  The "examples" fixed here would need to be done on hundreds of dissectors, so I'm not sure why Coverity is complaining about just this one.  And if it is complaining about hundreds of dissectors, changes need to be made to make Coverity understand the Wireshark API because these are not problems.

I understand your frustration. I had a look and I will update this part again, I'll remove `snprintf()`. README.developer has some hints...

Yes, Coverity does not understand `wmem` overall but it could be improved by using model file on the website.
I took care of it with !24208.  The only real "bug" was using wmem_strbuf_finalize() when wmem_strbuf_get_str() should have been used (and its good if Coverity can catch that.

Actually, I disagree with reverting back the whole lot. For example, I want to use `val_to_str_ext_const` and no need to add the hex value for Unknown... it's repeating too much. I don't see the point to change those back. It's worse now.

I agree with wmem_strbuf_finalize(), I would have used `wmem_strbuf_get_str()` too in my update I was preparing.
Actually, can we please not revert back the whole lot? I can fix the part with `snprintf` but I wish to keep the rest of my changes.
